title: Heavier or lighter on a balance scale
examples: How does a balance scale work?

left.label: Watermelon
left.ask: Why does the heavier side go down?

explain.say: A balance scale tells you which thing is heavier. Look at the board. The watermelon side goes down, because it is heavier. The pineapple side goes up.

draw.text: Heavier or lighter on a balance scale

left.label: Watermelon
left.ask: Why does the heavier side go down?

explain.say: Now find out how heavy the watermelon is. Put 4 weights of 1 kilogram on the other side. Now the beam is level. Level means both sides weigh the same. So the watermelon is 4 kilograms.

right.label: Four 1 kg weights
right.ask: What does it mean when the scale is level?

explain.say: Now look at a big pillow and a small brick. The brick side goes down. The pillow is full of soft stuffing and air, so it is light. A bigger thing can be lighter.
A kilogram is a unit for how heavy something is. Here a bag of flour balances a 1 kilogram weight. So the flour is 1 kilogram.
Look at the board. A 1 kilogram pineapple and a 3 kilogram bag of rice balance the watermelon. 1 and 3 make 4. What could you weigh at home?

faq.q: Why does the heavier side go down?
faq.a: Gravity pulls harder on the heavier side, so that pan sinks and the lighter pan rises. When both sides are equally heavy, the beam stays level.
asks: How does a balance scale work?

faq.a: No. A big pillow is full of air and feathers, so it is light. A small brick is packed with hard clay, so it is heavy. Only the scale can tell you.
asks: Can a small thing be heavy?

faq.a: A kilogram is a unit for measuring how heavy something is, its mass. A bag of sugar is often 1 kilogram, and a large watermelon can be about 4 kilograms.

faq.q: What does it mean when the scale is level?
faq.a: A level beam means both sides have the same mass. If 4 one-kilogram weights balance a watermelon, the watermelon is 4 kilograms.

faq.q: What is lighter than a kilogram?
faq.a: Small things are measured in grams. There are 1,000 grams in a kilogram, and an apple is about 150 grams.

facts: On a balance scale, the heavier side moves down and the lighter side moves up.
Balance scales were used in ancient Egypt more than 4,000 years ago.

quiz.say: On a balance, one pan goes down. The other pan goes up. Which pan holds the heavier thing?
quiz.show: ⚖️ One pan down, one pan up. Which is heavier?
quiz.why: The heavier thing pulls its pan down. The lighter pan goes up.

wrong.0: The pan that goes up holds the lighter thing.
wrong.2: Things that weigh the same keep the beam level.

quiz.say: A watermelon balances 4 weights of 1 kilogram. How heavy is the watermelon?
quiz.show: 🍉 balances 4 weights of 1 kg. How heavy?
quiz.why: A level beam means both sides weigh the same. 4 weights of 1 kilogram make 4 kilograms.

wrong.1: 1 kilogram is just one of the weights. There are 4.
wrong.2: 40 kilograms is far too heavy. Count the 4 weights.
